preamble: Voicing and spirantization of the voiceless velar stop [k] to the voiced velar fricative [ɣ]. In the Chukotkan branch of Chukotko-Kamchatkan, Proto-Chukotko-Kamchatkan word-initial *k became ɣ in the personal pronouns (Chukchi ɣəm 'I', ɣət 'you'), while Itelmen kept k. In Kikuyu, Dahl's law voicing dissimilation turned a Proto-Bantu *k into ɣ (spelled g) when the next syllable began with a voiceless consonant, as in gũtũ /ɣotò/ 'ear' and the language name Gĩkũyũ.

examples.to: Chukchi гым ɣəm, Koryak гыммо ɣəmmo, Alutor гыммы ɣəmmə
examples.note: Itelmen (Kamchatkan) keeps the stop: кәмма kəmma.

examples.to: Chukchi гыт ɣət, Alutor гытты ɣəttə
examples.note: Itelmen keeps the stop: кәзза kəzza.
Dahl's law: *k became ɣ (spelled g) before a syllable with a voiceless consonant, here t.
The prefix kĩ- surfaces as gĩ- [ɣe] before the voiceless k of the stem; the anglicized name Kikuyu reflects the unvoiced form.

sources: Fortescue, M. (2005). Comparative Chukotko-Kamchatkan Dictionary. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110925388
